subject: Anableps anableps
claim: The four-eyed fish has two eyes that are each functionally partitioned for aerial and aquatic viewing; the ventral hemiretina receiving the aerial field has a substantially greater ganglion-cell density and distinct opsin domains.
mechanism: split optical/retinal domains for two media
limitations: Functional partitioning does not imply four anatomical eyes.
contradictions: Popular descriptions calling Anableps literally four-eyed are anatomically misleading.

subject: Tripedalia cystophora box jellyfish
claim: Tripedalia cystophora has 24 eyes arranged on four rhopalia, with multiple eye types specialized for different visual functions rather than one uniform camera-like system.
mechanism: distributed multi-eye system with specialized lens and non-lens channels
limitations: Low temporal resolution in lens eyes should not be generalized to all eye types or all cubozoans.

sources.authors: Megan O'Connor; Dan-E Nilsson; Anders Garm

subject: Acanthopleura granulata chiton
claim: Acanthopleura granulata embeds hundreds of mineral eyes in its shell; aragonite lenses and retinas support coarse spatial vision in both air and water.
mechanism: mineral-lens eyes integrated into shell plates
limitations: Later optical work questions simple birefringence-based explanations of how the aragonite lens achieves its performance.
contradictions: The optical role of aragonite birefringence is more complex than early simplified accounts.

sources.title: A chiton uses aragonite lenses to form images
sources.authors: Daniel I Speiser; Douglas J Eernisse; Sönke Johnsen

subject: deep-sea fish hybrid photoreceptors
claim: Some deep-sea fish larvae have photoreceptors with rod-like morphology but cone-like molecular machinery, and Maurolicus retains a hybrid architecture into adulthood while other taxa transition toward rods.
mechanism: developmental decoupling of photoreceptor morphology and molecular identity
limitations: Functional performance of hybrid receptors varies by species and developmental stage.

sources.title: Deep-sea fish reveal an alternative developmental trajectory for vertebrate vision
sources.authors: Lily G Fogg; Stamatina Isari; Jonathan E Barnes; Jagdish Suresh Patel; N Justin Marshall; Walter Salzburger; Fanny de Busserolles; Fabio Cortesi

subject: Diretmus argenteus
claim: Diretmus argenteus possesses an extreme expansion of rod opsin genes and adults can express many RH1 variants simultaneously, consistent with spectral discrimination in dim bioluminescent environments.
limitations: Multiple RH1 opsins do not demonstrate a behavioral experience equivalent to '14 colors'.
contradictions: Popular claims equating opsin count with number of perceived colors are unsupported.

sources.title: Vision using multiple distinct rod opsins in deep-sea fishes

subject: Adelpha fessonia butterfly
claim: Although Adelpha fessonia is trichromatic, visual modeling suggests that some conspecific/comimetic wing patterns are not easily discriminated chromatically or achromatically by the butterfly itself or modeled avian predators.
limitations: Model-based discriminability does not prove which additional signals are used behaviorally.

sources.title: Trichromacy is insufficient for mate detection in a mimetic butterfly
sources.authors: Andrew Dang; Gary D Bernard; Furong Yuan; Aide Macias-Muñoz; Ryan I Hill; J P Lawrence; Aline Giselle Rangel Olguin; Armando Luis-Martínez; Sean P Mullen; Jorge Llorente-Bousquets; Adriana D Briscoe

subject: Ophiocoma wendtii brittle star
claim: Spatial vision can emerge from a body-wide photoreceptor network when expanded chromatophores provide optical screening; when the chromatophores contract in darkness, the spatial response disappears although the receptors remain.
mechanism: distributed extraocular photoreception plus chromatophore screening
limitations: Behavior and geometry support the mechanism, but downstream neural processing is not fully reconstructed.
contradictions: A related species with a similar photoreceptor network does not show the same spatial-vision behavior.

sources.title: Extraocular Vision in a Brittle Star Is Mediated by Chromatophore Movement in Response to Ambient Light
sources.authors: Lauren Sumner-Rooney; John D Kirwan; Elijah Lowe; Esther Ullrich-Lüter

subject: sabellid radiolar eyes
claim: Sabellid fan worms evolved peripheral compound eyes on feeding radioles; comparative work shows conserved c-opsin use with diversification of downstream G-protein repertoires among species.
mechanism: c-opsin phototransduction in peripheral compound eyes with species-specific signaling cascades
limitations: Transcript expression does not prove that every detected G-protein subunit is functionally engaged in every visual response.

subject: Diadema africanum sea urchin
claim: Diadema africanum shows coarse spatial vision without conventional eyes, consistent with distributed photoreception and body-level optical screening.
mechanism: distributed body photoreceptors plus screening by opaque structures
limitations: The dominant screening structure remains unresolved and spine density alone does not explain visual capability across species.

sources.title: The sea urchin Diadema africanum uses low resolution vision to find shelter and deter enemies
sources.authors: John D Kirwan; Michael J Bok; Jochen Smolka; James J Foster; José Carlos Hernández; Dan-Eric Nilsson

subject: scallop mirror eyes
claim: Scallops can carry up to about 200 image-forming eyes whose primary focusing element is a concave multilayer mirror of square guanine crystals rather than the weakly refracting lens; the mirror projects onto a double-layered retina that samples central and peripheral fields differently.
mechanism: hierarchical guanine-crystal multilayer mirror with dual retinal layers
function: spatial imaging around the mantle margin, with distinct retinal layers receiving different portions of the reflected image
limitations: The Science study establishes mirror architecture and image formation, but eye count and optical performance vary among scallop species; the popular analogy to a reflecting telescope is structurally useful, not evidence of telescope-like acuity.
contradictions: Popular descriptions can imply that scallops have telescope-level resolution; the paper instead demonstrates a reflecting optical architecture.

sources.title: The image-forming mirror in the eye of the scallop
sources.authors: Benjamin A Palmer; Gavin J Taylor; Vlad Brumfeld; Dvir Gur; Michal Shemesh; Nadav Elad; Aya Osherov; Dan Oron; Steve Weiner; Lia Addadi

subject: stomatopod dynamic polarization vision
claim: Gonodactylus smithii and Odontodactylus scyllarus actively rotate their stalked compound eyes torsionally so polarization-sensitive microvilli align to increase polarization contrast; this makes receptor orientation itself a dynamic part of sensing rather than a fixed sampling geometry.
mechanism: torsional eye rotation plus four microvillar polarization orientations in the dorsal/ventral hemispheres
function: active enhancement of linearly polarized object/background contrast during visual inspection
limitations: Experiments used controlled polarized stimuli and two stomatopod species; the ecological contribution of this mechanism across natural scenes and the full clade is not equivalent to demonstrating universally superior polarization discrimination.
contradictions: The often-repeated idea that stomatopod visual complexity automatically means superior general vision is misleading; this result demonstrates a specialized active polarization mechanism.

sources.title: Dynamic polarization vision in mantis shrimps
sources.authors: Ilse M Daly; Martin J How; Julian C Partridge; Shelby E Temple; N Justin Marshall; Thomas W Cronin; Nicholas W Roberts

subject: adult dragonfly regional compound-eye specialization
claim: Adult dragonfly compound eyes redistribute sampling resolution into behavior-specific foveae and foveal bands rather than maximizing acuity uniformly; in migratory Anax junius, enlarged dorsal ommatidia occupy roughly one third of the eye surface yet sample a comparatively narrow continuous strip of visual space across the dorsal field.
mechanism: regional variation in ommatidial diameter, interommatidial angle and optical-axis direction
function: behavior-dependent high-resolution sampling for prey/conspecific detection while preserving broad compound-eye coverage
limitations: The quantitative mapping is an older comparative morphological study; it demonstrates optical sampling specialization but does not by itself specify modern neural receptive-field resolution or temporal performance.
contradictions: A large compound eye should not be treated as uniformly high resolution: substantial surface area can be devoted to a narrow behaviorally relevant visual band.

sources.title: Development of the compound eyes of dragonflies (Odonata). III. Adult compound eyes
